samples.name: Hello World
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: A blocked evaluator verdict prevents the fake publishing tool from running and emits gate evidence.
samples.nonGuarantee: Only the configured lexical evaluator and local tool seam are covered; semantic or hosted-tool safety is not implied.
samples.benignControl: A clean testimonial executes once in the deterministic offline control.
samples.compositionRationale: Teaches the smallest individual tool-gate seam before introducing the aggregate builder.

samples.name: Enforcement Walkthrough
samples.description: Broad walkthrough of run, tool, session, moat, shadow, and output enforcement.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: Each demonstrated gate can prevent its scoped local effect and records content-minimized evidence.
samples.nonGuarantee: No single gate covers every attack, and live model behavior is not itself a pass oracle.
samples.benignControl: The walkthrough includes allowed or unchanged paths alongside blocked scenarios where the seam supports them.
samples.compositionRationale: Deliberately contrasts individual run, tool, shadow, and session middleware seams without stacking independent tool-gate registrations.

samples.name: MAF Support Agent
samples.description: Blocks a read-to-POST exfiltration sequence in a realistic support agent.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: The configured read-then-POST sequence is blocked before the fake exfiltration effect executes.
samples.nonGuarantee: The sequence policy does not classify arbitrary semantic intent or inspect provider-hosted tools.
samples.benignControl: Ordinary order lookup remains available without the guarded read-to-POST sequence.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses UseGatekeeper to install run scope, sequence enforcement, and evidence in one ordered composition.

samples.name: Tool Approval
samples.description: Auto-approves routine work and pauses risky calls for a human decision.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: Routine calls may continue while matching risky arguments produce a resumable approval request.
samples.nonGuarantee: Approval validates a human decision point, not the business correctness of the refund.
samples.benignControl: A small routine refund is auto-approved before the large-refund pause is demonstrated.
samples.compositionRationale: Teaches the dedicated MAF approval continuation seam, which has its own supported bridge.

samples.name: Beachhead and Tribunal
samples.description: Combines deterministic budgets and egress with a calibrated semantic boundary.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: Deterministic gates enforce their exact budgets and egress rules; judges enforce only after calibration clears promotion.
samples.nonGuarantee: Calibration-set success is not production generalization and local gates cannot control opaque provider tools.
samples.benignControl: Each scene retains an allowed or utility path appropriate to its protected boundary.
samples.compositionRationale: Every live Beachhead and Tribunal runtime scene uses the aggregate builder.

samples.name: Agent Harness Simple
samples.description: Caps an autonomous MAF Agent Harness loop.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: The local Harness tool loop cannot execute more than the configured Gatekeeper tool-call budget.
samples.nonGuarantee: The sample does not bound work hidden inside provider-hosted capabilities or prove task quality.
samples.benignControl: A Harness run that completes below the budget remains allowed.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses the aggregate builder to place a run-scoped budget around the real Harness.

samples.name: Agent Harness Defended
samples.description: Protects an autonomous support harness with budgets, sequence, and egress policy.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: Budget, sequence, and domain controls prevent the demonstrated fake Harness exfiltration effects.
samples.nonGuarantee: The stack covers declared local tools, not every possible semantic attack or hosted capability.
samples.benignControl: Legitimate bounded support work remains available within the configured policies.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses one aggregate builder for Harness budget, sequence, egress, scope, and evidence.

samples.name: Defense in Depth
samples.description: Exercises one indirect-injection campaign across run, tool, and result seams.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: A different enforced seam blocks each demonstrated stage before its fake harmful effect executes.
samples.nonGuarantee: The semantic judge requires representative calibration and deterministic gates cover only declared arguments and results.
samples.benignControl: Clean retrieval and on-domain, referentially valid support actions are the intended allowed path.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses one aggregate builder for call gates, result admission, run scope, and evidence.

samples.name: Output Panel
samples.description: Composes calibrated output axes with an advisory utility valve.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: Each promoted output axis reports independent evidence, while the utility valve remains advisory.
samples.nonGuarantee: Panel agreement is not a universal safety score and an unready judge is never silently promoted.
samples.benignControl: Benign useful output is checked against over-refusal pressure.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses the aggregate builder for the promoted post-run judge panel and evidence.

samples.name: Monetary and Per-Call Budget
samples.description: Bounds refund spray by call count and cumulative amount.
externalEffects: deterministic offline scripted provider and fake/local effects
optional configured Azure OpenAI overlay
samples.passOracle: Deterministic offline attack and benign-control assertions plus Gatekeeper evidence.
samples.guarantee: Per-tool count and monetary limits stop fake refunds beyond configured bounds.
samples.nonGuarantee: The gates do not determine whether an otherwise in-budget refund is legitimate.
samples.benignControl: Refunds within both count and amount limits remain allowed.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses the aggregate builder for each run-scoped financial budget stack.

samples.name: Explainability and Trust
samples.description: Explains verdict provenance, counterfactual replay, and honest trust aggregation.
externalEffects: offline path
optional configured Azure OpenAI judge call
samples.passOracle: Provenance, replay differences, and trust component availability.
samples.guarantee: Provenance, replay, and trust aggregation expose exactly which evidence is available and changed.
samples.nonGuarantee: A composite trust score never substitutes missing axes or proves causal safety.
samples.benignControl: The replay includes an unchanged or allowed comparison configuration.
samples.compositionRationale: Exercises replay, provenance, and evidence APIs directly rather than a layered runtime composition.

samples.name: Real A2A Boundary
samples.description: Calibrates and guards both directions of an explicitly authorized A2A call.
externalEffects: configured Azure OpenAI calibration/judge calls
authorized remote A2A request
samples.passOracle: Both calibration reports pass before one guarded endpoint response is observed.
samples.guarantee: Both calibrated boundary gates wrap one explicitly authorized remote A2A request; caller time and response buffering are bounded.
samples.nonGuarantee: The client cannot set the remote provider token cap or intercept the remote agent internal tools.
samples.benignControl: A concise on-goal capability request is the benign delegation.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses the aggregate builder at the real A2A run boundary.

samples.name: A2A Calibration
samples.description: Calibrates both A2A judge axes without contacting an A2A endpoint.
externalEffects: consented configured Azure OpenAI calibration calls
samples.passOracle: Calibration accuracy, false-positive, baseline, and inline-readiness bars.
samples.guarantee: Promotion is refused unless both A2A axes clear the declared calibration thresholds.
samples.nonGuarantee: The calibration corpus is not held-out production evidence and no remote endpoint is exercised.
samples.benignControl: Benign hard negatives measure false-positive behavior for both axes.
samples.compositionRationale: Calibrates judge axes directly and does not construct an enforcement stack.

samples.name: Mocked Dangerous Tools
samples.description: Offline SQL, browser, cloud, and package contract design fixture.
externalEffects: none; fake components only
samples.passOracle: Allowed fixtures execute and hostile fixtures leave fake effects at zero.
samples.guarantee: Hostile fixture calls leave every fake SQL, browser, cloud, and package effect at zero while allowed fixtures execute.
samples.nonGuarantee: Sample-local contracts demonstrate policy shape and do not claim production parser coverage.
samples.benignControl: Four explicitly allowed fixture calls execute successfully.
samples.compositionRationale: Calls deterministic gates as isolated contract fixtures to expose exact allow and block behavior.

samples.name: Poisoned Tool Kill Chain
samples.description: Contains a poisoned fake MCP source and blocks the downstream attack chain.
externalEffects: none; fake MCP, email, HTTP, delete, and propagation effects
samples.passOracle: Poison is withheld, containment is active, and every harmful effect counter remains zero.
samples.guarantee: Poison is withheld, the fake source is contained, and bulk-read, email, HTTP, delete, and propagation effects stay zero.
samples.nonGuarantee: The sample does not claim control of a real MCP server process or network.
samples.benignControl: A clean bounded tool path remains usable before containment.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses one aggregate stack for the poisoned-tool kill chain and clean control.

samples.name: Harness-Owned Tool Misuse
samples.description: Discovers and blocks misuse of a real runtime-injected Harness capability.
externalEffects: none; scripted model and local fake effects
samples.passOracle: Runtime name is discovered, hostile effect remains zero, benign control succeeds.
samples.guarantee: Misuse of the runtime-discovered Harness capability is blocked before execution.
samples.nonGuarantee: The policy does not infer every harmful user intent and covers the discovered local capability only.
samples.benignControl: A normal one-sentence ticket summary succeeds without a gate block.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses one aggregate stack around Harness-owned tool calls.

samples.name: Jailbreak and Tool Abuse
samples.description: Contrasts an obvious input block with contracts that survive paraphrase.
externalEffects: none; scripted proposals and fake effects
samples.passOracle: Obvious attack stops pre-model; paraphrases are stopped by contracts; benign control executes.
samples.guarantee: Obvious jailbreak text stops pre-model and paraphrased abuse is blocked by authoritative tool contracts.
samples.nonGuarantee: Lexical jailbreak detection alone is not claimed to resist paraphrase or novel attacks.
samples.benignControl: A single-customer status lookup executes and returns useful output.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses aggregate pre-run and tool-call compositions for jailbreak and abuse scenarios.

samples.name: Tool Result Admission
samples.description: Masks a fake credential and truncates diagnostics before model context.
externalEffects: none; local fake results
samples.passOracle: Secret is absent, oversized content is bounded, and clean content is unchanged.
samples.guarantee: Fake credentials are masked and oversized diagnostics are truncated before re-entering model context.
samples.nonGuarantee: The result gates do not establish truthfulness or semantic safety of all admitted content.
samples.benignControl: A clean bounded diagnostic result passes through unchanged.
samples.compositionRationale: Uses the aggregate builder for tool-result admission and evidence.

samples.name: Hosted Tool Coverage Boundary
samples.description: Proves provider-hosted execution stays outside local tool-gate coverage.
externalEffects: none; provider-hosted tool is never invoked
samples.passOracle: Unacknowledged risk refuses promotion and acknowledgment never increases structural coverage.
samples.guarantee: Promotion refuses unacknowledged opaque hosted execution and acknowledgment never inflates structural coverage.
samples.nonGuarantee: Acknowledging risk does not intercept, sandbox, or observe provider-hosted execution.
samples.benignControl: A local-tool-only inventory remains the fully interceptable comparison case.
samples.compositionRationale: Exercises the coverage analyzer directly because no runtime gate stack is constructed.
